whatToWatch.text: The defense showed up in Week 1 — 10 points allowed and three sacks — and now it heads to Arizona to prove it wasn't a one-week mirage against a Cardinals unit that's been stingy too (14 points allowed, three sacks of their own).

That 41.5 total says Vegas expects a grinder, and the 4.5-point spread says Seattle should still walk out of the desert 2-0 — road wins in this division are how you build a season, not a highlight reel.

Injury watch matters here: one Seahawk is out and four are questionable, with Ty Okada, Nick Emmanwori and Tory Horton among the names to track, while Arizona is dealing with its own absence and question marks around Garrett Williams and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson.

newsBlurb.text: Drew Lock takes the reins in Arizona with Sam Darnold sidelined, and nobody's sure whether the injury costs Seattle one week or three. Lock looked steady in relief against New England, where the defense flipped last year's Week 1 script and closed out a 13-10 comeback instead of coughing it up late. Now Mike Macdonald's group finds out if that formula travels on the road — and Terrion Arnold's new deal gives the secondary another piece to lean on.

predictor.disclaimer: For entertainment/informational purposes only — not betting advice.

Brissett's 221.5 passing yards sits at even money on both sides with the line untouched from open, and with just one game played this season there's no real trend here to lean on — on the road against a Cardinals defense allowing 14 points a game with 3 sacks per game, it's basically a coin flip as priced.
Brissett's rushing line sits at 11.5 with even money (+100) both ways and no movement off the open, and with only one game played this season there's no real trend here to lean on either direction.
Love's line hasn't budged from 35.5 with even +100 juice both ways, and with just one game played this season there's no real trend here to lean on — the under side is a coin flip on paper.
